Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second half! Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das are the openers. Chris Woakes to begin. Here we go...
... RUN CHASE ...

Bangladesh will be happy with the late comeback but the damage was done earlier by England. Bangladesh opted to bowl first and started well. The ball was swinging but failed to get any wickets in the first 10 overs. Bangladesh then introduced their spin duo in the middle phase but England counter-attacked and didn't allow to settle them. However, Bangladesh will be happy with how they fought back. There is still a lot in this pitch but Bangladeshi batters are in good touch. They need someone to play a big innings. Can Bangladesh chase it down or it will be two losses in two for the defending champions?

Jos Buttler did mention a lot after their first game that they were short of runs but England though have got the job done this time around as 364 does look like a winning total on this pitch. Excellent stuff from the defending champions. The top three were fabulous first of all. The openers got them off to a flier, Jonny Bairstow fell after his fifty but Malan and Root quickly put on a big stand of 151-runs to get England to a big total. However, there were slight hiccups as England started to fall apart in the fag end but somehow got crucial runs in the end to get over 360. Still, at one point 400 was looking gettable but England will be happy with this score.
BYE! Very full and on leg, Wood swings across but misses. The keeper throws it at the batter's end but Reece Topley completes the run. ENGLAND END WITH 364.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set and it is time for the national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first followed by the English side. Done with all the pre-match proceedings. It is time for action. Jonny Bairstow, who is playing his 100th ODI match walks out along with Dawid Malan. The Bangla Tigers are all set as well. Mustafizur Rahman to steam in first. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Shaun Pollock says it is challenging for the fielders in the outfield if they dive. Dinesh Karthik later adds the color of the pitch is light brown because there has been a lot of rain in the night. The grass has been cut too which the seamers won't like much. Reckons the pitch is going to be slow in nature and hard to score runs.
England (PLAYING XI) - Jonny Bairstow, Dawid Malan, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Jos Buttler (C/WK), Liam Livingstone, Sam Curran, Chris Woakes, Adil Rashid, Mark Wood, Reece Topley (In for Moeen Ali).

Bangladesh (PLAYING XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Shakib Al Hasan (C), Mehidy Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim(WK), Towhid Hridoy, Mahedi Hasan, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, Mustafizur Rahman.

Jos Buttler says they would have bowled first as well. Informs Reece Topley comes in for Moeen Ali. Adds it was a bad day against New Zealand but are looking forward to put in a good performance today.

Shakib Al Hasan says they will bowl first. Hopes his seamers can get something out of the surface. Reckons they didn't start well in the first match but the belief was always there and it was pleasing to see. Shares this is a different game but they want to be as calm as possible. Tells Mehidy Hasan is a leader in this team. England are world champions but they have to be at their best today.
